builder_plan.scenario: A product assistant retrieves plausible documents but gives unsupported answers.
builder_plan.change: Change one retrieval or ranking step while keeping the document snapshot fixed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retrieval pipeline with identical questions and answer model.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Supported answers, retrieval misses, correct abstentions, index cost, and response latency.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Utility-Aware Generative Recommendation: Utility-Enriched Semantic Codes and Utility-Guided Decoding
summary: Replaces purely semantic SID construction and likelihood-only beam scoring in generative recommendation with utility-enriched semantic codes and beam scores augmented by predicted post-exposure utility. Costs include maintaining per-item utility estimates with incremental updates and training multiple post-exposure outcome predictors, though SID length, vocabulary, and decoding cost are unchanged. Can fail if utility predictors are inaccurate or drift faster than incremental code updates, causing beam scoring to mis-rank candidates, and the reported gain presupposes an existing deployed generative recommendation pipeline at platform scale.
rationale: The method requires a production generative recommendation system with logged post-exposure behavior data and online serving infrastructure, which a small team with a single GPU typically lacks, making the reported 0.206% watch-time gain unreplicable in their setting.
technique: Utility-guided beam decoding for generative recommendation

claims.statement: Replaces purely semantic SID construction and likelihood-only beam scoring in generative recommendation with utility-enriched semantic codes and beam scores augmented by predicted post-exposure utility. Costs include maintaining per-item utility estimates with incremental updates and training multiple post-exposure outcome predictors, though SID length, vocabulary, and decoding cost are unchanged. Can fail if utility predictors are inaccurate or drift faster than incremental code updates, causing beam scoring to mis-rank candidates, and the reported gain presupposes an existing deployed generative recommendation pipeline at platform scale.
Online A/B test on Kuaishou reports a 0.206% increase in video watch time; no multiplicative factor is given.
